newsitem.title: USA: NYC comptroller subpoenas Queens' library records.
newsitem.headline: NYC comptroller subpoenas Queens' library records.

text.p: The New York City comptroller, in an unprecedented step, on Monday said he had subpoenaed records from the Queens Borough Public Library to force it to account for how it spent some public funds.

Alan Hevesi last week said the library had blocked his auditors from reviewing its corporate fund, where public money was not properly recorded from 1975 to 1991. Around $8 million remains in the fund.
Saying this was the first time the comptroller ever had to subpoena records from a public entity, Hevesi asked what is "Queens Borough Public Library hiding?" in prepared remarks.
He added that by preventing the audit, the library officials had created an appearnce of impropriety.
The city funds more than 80 percent of the library's budget, and the library should be accountable to the taxpayers, Hevesi wrote.
The library could not be reached for comment.
